title: App Runner and Elastic Beanstalk: what remains, and when they fit

videos.script: Every lesson so far has handed you parts. Instances, groups, load balancers, task definitions. This one is about two services that assemble the parts for you. {{two}} App Runner takes an image or a Git repository and gives back an address. It closed to new customers on the thirtieth of April, 2026, and moto does not imitate it. So that half is taught from AWS's documentation, with its prices from Virginia, and nothing in it was run. {{meters}} You will see why its bill has two meters. Memory runs all day. The processor runs only while it serves. {{beanstalk}} Elastic Beanstalk is older, and still open. It builds EC2 instances, a group and a load balancer, in your own account. moto keeps its application and its environment as records. You will ask for the machines behind them and get four empty lists. {{remains}} Then the part a platform does not take away. How a new version reaches the instances, which platform version they run, where the logs go. {{fit}} And last, when a small team should choose one of these, and the signs that it is time to leave.
